item.title: Canal City Hakata: Shopping and Fountains — Guide
item.description: Canal City Hakata is one of Fukuoka’s landmark shopping and entertainment complexes, a huge, boldly designed ‘city within the city’ built around a curving artificial canal that winds through its centre. Its colourful, tiered buildings house hundreds of shops and boutiques, restaurants and cafes, a cinema, theatres, hotels, and the popular Ramen Stadium where several regional ramen makers gather on one floor. The signature draw is the canal itself, where regular fountain shows send water dancing to music and light, especially impressive after dark.

item.title: Hakata Gion Yamakasa Festival — Guide
item.description: The Hakata Gion Yamakasa is Fukuoka’s most famous and thrilling festival, a tradition over 700 years old held every July, centred on Kushida Shrine. Over two weeks, ornate decorative floats (kazariyama) are displayed around the city, but the real drama is the racing floats (kakiyama) — one-tonne portable shrines carried on the shoulders of teams of men in traditional loincloths. It climaxes before dawn on July 15 with the ‘Oiyama’, when the teams charge a roughly 5-kilometre course through the streets of Hakata at a flat sprint, water thrown over them by cheering crowds, racing against the clock in a spectacle of raw energy, sweat and community pride.

item.title: Hakata Machiya Folk Museum — Guide
item.description: The Hakata Machiya Folk Museum, right across from Kushida Shrine, offers an engaging window into the life and culture of old Hakata. Housed in restored machiya — traditional wooden townhouses from the Meiji era — it recreates the world of the district’s merchants and craftsmen a century ago, with period rooms, everyday objects and exhibits on Hakata’s history and its great Yamakasa festival. You can also see demonstrations of the region’s traditional crafts, including Hakata-ori silk weaving and the making of Hakata dolls, and often try simple hands-on activities.

item.title: Kushida Shrine: The Heart of Old Hakata — Guide
item.description: Kushida Shrine is the tutelary shrine of the old merchant district of Hakata and one of the most beloved shrines in Fukuoka. Founded over a thousand years ago and affectionately called ‘O-Kushida-san’, it is the spiritual centre of Hakata life and the starting point of the city’s greatest festival, the Hakata Gion Yamakasa. Even outside the July festival, you can see a towering, elaborately decorated kazariyama float on permanent display in the grounds, giving a sense of the festival’s scale year-round.

item.title: Mentaiko: Fukuoka's Spicy Cod Roe — Guide
item.description: Mentaiko — spicy marinated pollock (or cod) roe — is one of Fukuoka’s most iconic foods, and the city of Hakata is considered its Japanese home. The roe sacs are cured in a marinade of chilli, and sometimes sake and other seasonings, giving a savoury, salty, gently spicy flavour and a distinctive popping texture from the tiny eggs. It is endlessly versatile: eaten simply with hot rice, grilled, stuffed into rice balls, blended into creamy mentaiko pasta (a Japanese invention), added to toast, and used across the region’s cooking.

item.title: Tochoji Temple and the Great Wooden Buddha — Guide
item.description: Tochoji is one of the oldest and most important temples in Fukuoka, founded by the great monk Kobo Daishi (Kukai) in the ninth century, making it central to Shingon Buddhism in the region. In the heart of Hakata, its grounds hold a striking vermilion five-storey pagoda and its greatest treasure: the Fukuoka Daibutsu, a magnificent seated wooden Buddha over 10 metres tall and one of the largest of its kind in Japan, carved from a single camphor tree.
